reconcile.connective: Defenders read the Chronicler's "sons of Manasseh" as loose for "descendants" — so Zelophehad is still Hepher's son, just listed farther down a compressed line.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible), who sets the two genealogies side by side: Numbers and Joshua make Zelophehad the son of Hepher, while 1 Chronicles drops Hepher and lists him among the sons of Manasseh.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The sons of Manasseh—or descendants; for Ashriel was a grandson, and Zelophehad was a generation farther removed in descent (Num 26:33). The text, as it stands, is so confused and complicated that it is exceedingly difficult to trace the genealogical thread, and a great variety of conjectures have been made with a view to clear away the obscurity.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly engages the 1 Chr 7:14-15 listing that the skeptic uses: reads 'sons of Manasseh' as 'descendants', explicitly places Zelophehad 'a generation farther removed in descent' citing Num 26:33, so the Hepher line is preserved and the Chronicles wording is compression, not a rival paternity. The single note that names Zelophehad and resolves this exact tension.

excerpts.excerpt_text: hence we see that in many cases grandsons are called sons, and both are often confounded in the genealogical tables.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States the underlying harmonizing principle the row turns on — that in the genealogical tables 'sons' routinely means descendants/grandsons — which is exactly the move that lets 'sons of Manasseh' in 1 Chr 7:14 cover the multi-generation Hepher line of Num 27:1/Josh 17:3. Anchor block; on-tension sentence is deep in a note that surveys the Benjamin tables, but the principle is cited under 1 Chr 7:14-15. (Excludes the same note's 'endless... useless' aside, which declines to reconcile rather than harmonizing.)

pd_work.note: Treats this passage directly: reads the Chronicler's 'sons of Manasseh' as 'descendants' and places Zelophehad 'a generation farther removed in descent' (Num 26:33), preserving the Hepher line of Numbers and Joshua. Used as the textual anchor because Haley's coverage of this specific genealogy pair could not be confirmed; this is a harmonizing commentator surfaced on the row and keyed to the passage.
